summary.intent: Execute Phase 23 (rust-sdk-extraction) of the cipher-box project, extracting Rust crypto/core/API/FUSE/SDK code from the desktop app into a Cargo workspace with independent crates, then address verification gaps via gap closure planning.
summary.outcome: All 7 plans executed across 4 waves successfully (with a Wave 3 retry after usage limit interruption). Two verification gaps identified: orphaned desktop FUSE files (fixed inline via /simplify) and missing Windows WinFsp extraction (deferred to gap closure plan 23.1).

repo: cipher-box uses a GSD (get-shit-done) agentic workflow system with wave-based parallel plan execution, subagent spawning, and structured SUMMARY/VERIFICATION/STATE markdown artifacts
Phase 23 created a Cargo workspace at repo root with 5 new crates: cipherbox-crypto, cipherbox-core, cipherbox-api-client, cipherbox-fuse, cipherbox-sdk
The desktop app (apps/desktop/src-tauri) was refactored to a thin Tauri wrapper — commands/, tray/, main.rs, plus thin fuse/mod.rs and sync/mod.rs bridges
9 orphaned FUSE files existed in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/ with no mod declarations — dead code never compiled, safe to delete

Windows WinFsp platform code was NOT extracted during Phase 23 — crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/ directory is missing despite pub mod windows behind a feature flag, creating a latent compilation bug
Cross-language test vectors (9 JSON files) added for Rust/TypeScript parity testing of crypto primitives

code.finding: Double HashMap lookup bug: open_files.get(&fh) called twice — once to set has_temp bool, again for the actual read. Consolidated to single lookup during /simplify.
Misleading #[allow(dead_code)] on the implementation module — it IS actively used by read_ops, write_ops, and dir_ops within the crate. Attribute removed.

9 files (cache.rs, constants.rs, dir_ops.rs, file_handle.rs, helpers.rs, inode.rs, operations.rs, read_ops.rs, write_ops.rs) were on disk but never compiled — no mod declarations in fuse/mod.rs. Deleted (-4,268 lines).

workflow: GSD wave-based execution: Wave 3 agents hit usage limit mid-execution, leaving partial crate directories with no lib.rs. On resume, agents were re-spawned and completed successfully — GSD's SUMMARY.md-based completion detection handled resumption cleanly
Parallel agents in the same wave can have interleaved git commits (observed in Wave 2 with 23-02/23-03) — no correctness impact but staging overlaps are possible
The /simplify skill triggered three parallel review agents (reuse, quality, efficiency) against the full phase diff — effective for catching moved-but-not-compiled dead code and double-lookup bugs
Gap closure flow: VERIFICATION.md gaps → /gsd:plan-phase --gaps reads gaps → creates gap_closure plans → execute-phase --gaps-only re-runs verifier
The classifyHandoffIfNeeded Claude Code runtime bug can cause agents to report 'failed' after completing all work — spot-check SUMMARY.md + git commits to determine true status

friction: Wave 3 agents (23-04, 23-05) hit usage limit mid-execution, requiring manual 'resume' and full agent re-spawn — partial uncommitted state had to be diagnosed before retry
Usage limit interruption left crate directories partially populated (Cargo.toml present, lib.rs missing) — required manual inspection of git log and working tree to assess recovery state
open_items: Gap closure plan 23.1: Extract Windows WinFsp operations (5 files, 2,824 LOC) from apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/windows/ into crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/ — currently a latent compilation bug (feature flag declared but directory missing)
The gsd-planner subagent was spawned at end of transcript for 23 --gaps but the plan content was not shown — gap closure plan(s) are in-progress/pending execution
Verification score was 3/5 must-haves — the two partial items (orphaned files fixed, Windows not extracted) should be re-verified after gap closure execution
